## Daily Sleep Scores and Sleep Apnea Events (March 1–7, 2026)
| Date       | Sleep Score | Sleep Apnea Events |
|------------|-------------|--------------------|
| 2026-03-01 | 82          | 1                  |
| 2026-03-02 | 75          | 1                  |
| 2026-03-03 | 78          | 1                  |
| 2026-03-04 | 45          | 2                  |
| 2026-03-05 | 80          | 1                  |
| 2026-03-06 | 50          | 2                  |
| 2026-03-07 | 72          | 1                  |

## Correlation Analysis
- A Pearson correlation coefficient calculated from the 7-day period yields r ≈ –0.97, indicating a very strong negative linear relationship.
- Days with the lowest sleep scores (45 and 50) consistently recorded 2 apnea events, while all other days (sleep scores 72–82) had only 1 event.
- **Conclusion:** The data strongly suggest that lower sleep scores are associated with a higher frequency of sleep apnea events. However, the sample is small (n=7), so the correlation should be interpreted with caution and ideally confirmed over a longer timeframe.
